evidence: STRUCTURE (supports a graded spread): task/tests/scoring.toml is byte-identical to the template (gates render/constraints 0.0; weights functional 0.6, polish 0.2, visual 0.2; floor functional 0.05); score.py and test.sh are byte-identical to the template. scored/functional/judge.toml uses aggregation weighted_mean over 43 binary criteria totalling weight 58.5; the largest single criterion (2.5) is 4.3% of functional; weight spreads across protocols (B 17.1%, T 16.2%, M 8.5%, L 8.5%, R 7.7%, K 6.8%, U 6.0%, C 4.3%, V 4.3%, S 3.4%, Z/U 3.4%, A 2.6%, D 2.6%, N/R-N/R-K 1.7% each, T/K 0.9%). polish: 5 binary weighted_mean (weights 3,3,2,1.5,2.5 of 12). visual: 5 likert points=5 with anchors, equal weight 1.2. Functional prompt.md:13 explicitly prevents single-precondition collapse beyond the global backend check: 'score EACH criterion independently, continue after failures ... A failed sibling verdict is not evidence against another row. Shared protocols reduce setup; they are not conjunctive bundles. When a setup step fails, set up the same thing again on a new job'. prompt.md:39 gives a fallback (Tomas's seeded conversation) so T/U/K rows do not collapse if candidate linking fails (owned only by hro_candidate_linked). Polish/visual prompts (polish prompt.md:12,18; visual prompt.md:12,16) state independent grading after the gate. Thought experiments: (a) board-only app with permissions but no conversations/live updates: passes gates, functional roughly 50-60% of weight, polish ~2/12-4.5/12, visual mid-likert -> mid reward; (b) full app lacking live push: loses hro_live_board, hro_msg_exchange-reply, unread/seen live rows and both polish live rows (6/12) -> visibly below golden but well above floor; (c) app with only job open/add candidate (passes gates): functional ~1/58.5 = 0.017 <= floor 0.05 -> reward 0, which is the intended floor exclusion, not collapse. So the rubric is designed to produce a spread, not all-or-nothing. All-or-nothing collapse points remain: (1) hro_gate_shared requires open job + add candidate + independent-context Observer readback, a deliberate dead-app gate; a job-only partial app scores 0 (policy-endorsed). (2) test.sh:224-226 - if the scored suite exceeds its 11100 s budget or rewardkit errors (one batched functional judge for 43 criteria with a 9000 s timeout over 14 protocols and many independent contexts), run_suite fails, test.sh exits leaving the gates-stage reward.json whose scored dimensions are 0 and floors_passed 0 -> reward 0 regardless of partial quality. This is template behavior (not a task defect) but makes discrimination contingent on the very long functional judge actually completing, which is unmeasured. MEASUREMENT: qc/README.md:27 requires an observed runtime-evidence.json record keyed reward_is_graded_not_binary_and_discriminates; none exists for input f53d9ed6... (no runtime-evidence.json in qc/runs/hireops-workspace-2026-10-03-r3; grep for the input hash in any runtime-evidence.json returned nothing). raw-evidence-index.json scope states verbatim: 'Full configured grading/workload, reward discrimination/ranking and Oracle/target scores are absent.' The scripted golden driver is not a judge run and produced no rewards for mutated/partial apps. Therefore the spread is plausible by design but not observed; per SKILL.md this cannot be upgraded to Pass and the missing required measurement keeps risk=true.
counterexample: Not a demonstrated defect. Unmeasured risk scenario: a conforming partial app (board, roles, notes, conversations correct, no live push) where the single batched functional judge (43 criteria, 14 sequential protocols, timeout 9000 s, suite budget 11100 s) times out or emits malformed verdicts; test.sh:224-226 then leaves reward 0 identical to a dead app, collapsing the spread. Whether this happens is unknown because no configured judge run or weak-app discrimination run exists for this input.
suggested_fix: Run the full configured verifier on the golden plus at least two hash-recorded mutated weak apps (e.g. live push removed; permissions removed) and record the resulting reward spread and durations in runtime-evidence.json under reward_is_graded_not_binary_and_discriminates; do not alter shared scoring/test.sh.
